correctness.rationale: The exact cyclic Dirichlet gap law and sine-product identity give a uniform radial cubic-plus-quintic area expansion. The zero set is six edges; the four vertex sectors give t and t^(5/3), while nonvertex edge neighborhoods contribute O(t^2). On the shape simplex, h^-1 and h^-5/3 are integrable, giving dominated convergence and the exact coefficients; radial Jacobian proves the conditional marked law. Direct Monte Carlo and independently evaluated integrals are consistent. Remaining risk is a hidden boundary-regime contribution, controlled by the stated vertex cutoff and edge estimates.

value.rationale: The natural four-point cyclic polygon small-area event has a previously unresolved sharp noninteger second-order tail and a concrete three-gap conditional geometry. It distinguishes all-four collapse (order t) from two-cluster degeneracy (order t^2), provides an exact positive double-integral coefficient, and yields an explicit normalized shape law useful for geometric probability and rare-event sampling. Not a routine computation of an already tabulated invariant.
